Dewy Bears
Ad Lab

Twenty four Instagram ads for a skin gummy brand with six flavours. Four funnel phases, eight A/B rounds of three cells, one variable per round. Every flavour gets four ads, so no single pouch carries the brand.

Approach

How I build an ad set

The same four steps for any brand. The ads below are what the steps produce once the buyer, the levers and the test plan are agreed.

01

Learn the buyer first

Audience, price band and product range before the first headline. Here that is women aged 25 to 40 in the Netherlands who care about their skin and enjoy a sweet treat, shopping six flavours at €29 a pouch.

02

Pick the lever, then write

Every ad keeps the brand's existing tone of voice and adds one psychological lever and two emotional triggers to it: identity, cost per use, endowment, social proof. The copy follows the lever, so each variant tests a separate idea.

03

Build the system once

Four layouts, one palette, one wordmark. Each layout has its own photo style: splash campaign shots for awareness, conversion and retargeting, and studio pack shots for the round 3 angle test. Within a round, the layout and photo stay fixed, so the message is the only thing a test reads.

04

Test one variable at a time

Each round has one variable, one primary read and one guardrail. The winning message carries forward and the products rotate, so every flavour gets read.

Brand

Candy gloss

Dewy Bears sells skin gummies in six fruit flavours. The look is a glossy pouch tilted in a juice splash, translucent bears and cut fruit. Each flavour owns its colour world. The voice is playful and plain: ingredients appear as contents, never as promises.

Catalogue

Six flavours, four ads each

Each pouch appears in exactly four cells. Round 2 picks the hero flavour from test results.

Layouts

Four layouts, four jobs

Each layout takes its name from the sweet shop world the brand lives in. The funnel phase sets which layout an ad uses, and the lever behind it shapes the words.

Fixed signal

Wordmark on every ad

Lilita One, stacked, in cream on photos and plum on paper.

Fixed signal

The flavour sets the colour

Fruit, bears, splash and pouch share one tint. The page never recolours a product.

Fixed signal

Hot pink tape

The first strip is always hot pink. It is the brand's handwriting across all four layouts.

Fixed signal

Short on the image

No more than eight words on a photo. Detail goes in the caption, where people read it.

Test map

Eight rounds, one variable each

Each round is a Meta A/B test with three cells and an even budget split.

RoundPhaseA/B formatVariableAudiencePrimary readGuardrail
Method

How a round is run

Meta A/B test for every round

Meta splits the audience so cells never overlap. Flexible ads mix creative on their own and hide which element won, so they come in after a winner exists.

Seven to thirty days per round

Seven days is the floor, so weekday and weekend behaviour both count. The round closes once each cell reaches its conversion target, within 30 days. Results in the first days are unstable, so no winner is called before the round closes.

Even budget, enough results

Cells share the round budget evenly. A winner is called once each cell has roughly 25 to 50 of its target event.

Winner carries forward

The next round holds the winning message and changes the next variable. Every new idea is tested against the current winner.

Optimise on what Meta can learn from

Meta's delivery learns once an ad set reaches about 50 optimisation events in a week. Until purchases reach that, rounds optimise on add to cart or landing page views, and purchases are read as the result.

Call winners on confidence

Meta reports how likely the winning cell is to win again. A low score counts as a tie, and the current winner stays.
